title: Cathy Chamberlain and the Rag-and-Roll Revue
summary: He joined her revue after rehearsals and got her the Ryan's job.

bands.name: Bob Catwell and His Seven Saturday Night Stompers

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I see... Well, okay... How did you get with Cathy Chamberlain, who a writer has called here "the queen of Rag-and-Roll"? How did you meet up with her and start playing?

Well, somebody had told her about me. The people she wanted to use had let down... I think they hadn't worked together or something. She had one or two (?) who was talking about who was who, how likely to work with me, and what they're going to open up with and what was they
going to do, you know... So we got together and had a rehearsal at some studio she rented out. She rented a studio on 45th Street and Eighth Avenue. We had a rehearsal two or three times.

We made this Rag-and-Roll Revue. She named it the Rag-and-Roll Revue, but she... She featured me a whole lot, you know. And in fact, we... We didn't record it, but we were working on stage, we worked together. We'd do things like, oh, let's see... "Jelly-Roll"... Like, "I ain't gonna do ...(?)... my jelly-roll" just by myself. And what else ....(?). Oh, "All Of Me." But anyway, she was doing things where we worked together. She'd sing one chorus of it and I'd sing the second chorus, then I'd sing the third chorus, but I put a little punch-line into the song that... That wasn't the name of it. I just put that punch-line there. "Flat-foot floogie with the floy joy," I'd put that in there.

In other words, she is a stylist who, even though she is a young woman, in her early thirties now, and at the time, in '76 or '78, she was singing music hearkening back to the 1920's, and she admires Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey and early Victoria Spivey and Ida Cox and those people...

Well, she... See, I know the difference. I met her... I got her a job where she is now, at Jimmy Ryan's. She's down at Jimmy Ryan's now. She's got seven pieces down there. I got her that job, and helped her get the men together, you know.

And in fact, she wanted me... I'm the first one she called to go down there and work with her. I was working down there on Saturday night with Bob Catwell(?) and His Seven Saturday Night Stompers. I was working with him. And he told the boss. He said, "Well, I think Freddie's too good. He's taking all the glamour(?) from you, and you won't..." If Freddie gets on it, gets back there with you, they ain't gonna pay you no mind -- they're going to look at him. So he says, "No, it's not a good idea; let Freddie stay where he is. You just go on your own." She tried her best to get me on drums. She even told the boss. She called me first. "I've got Freddie Moore on drums." "Who?" "Freddie Moore." "Oh, no, no. Don't get him. He's the main attraction Saturday night with Bob Catwell(?). You've got to take... Otherwise, you take him out of the band, or the band..." Blah-blah-blah. That's the way it went.
But she's down there now, and she's doing pretty good down there.
